description:
We are RWS NOVA INNOVATORS, a team of curious students from Reeds World School, driven by a shared interest in space technology, agriculture, and innovative problem-solving. 
Our challenge, “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data,” inspires us to explore how NASA’s Earth observation data can help farmers adapt to changing environmental conditions, make informed decisions, and build more resilient agricultural practices.
summary:
FieldShift is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform that helps farmers make informed decisions about crop rotation, irrigation, and field management using real-time and historical satellite and weather data.

The platform integrates five years of NASA POWER rainfall and temperature records, NASA GIBS MODIS Terra NDVI satellite imagery, Meteomatics soil moisture and evapotranspiration data, and Open-Meteo terrain information. By combining these datasets, FieldShift identifies vegetation health, soil moisture conditions, erosion-prone areas, and potential climate risks. It translates complex Earth observation data into practical field recommendations, including crop rotation alternatives, irrigation guidance, and timely responses to drought, heat, frost, and runoff risks. Its interactive Pipori Field Advisor further helps farmers understand conditions and explore suitable actions.

FieldShift addresses the challenge by making NASA's Earth observation data accessible and actionable for everyday farming decisions. It aims to promote climate-resilient agriculture, improve resource efficiency, reduce crop losses, and support sustainable farming practices.
details: Built by Team RWS NOVA INNOVATORS for the NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data"), FieldShift is a practical web app that helps farmers adapt their crop rotations and daily farm decisions using real satellite and weather data. We built the PHP backend and CSS styling ourselves, used Claude and Gemini to put together the interactive JavaScript, API integrations, and the Pipori Field Advisor, and relied on VS Code for coding and testing everything along the way. The platform pulls together 5-year NASA POWER rainfall and temperature records, 8-day NASA GIBS MODIS Terra NDVI satellite vegetation layers, Meteomatics temperature, evapotranspiration, and -15 cm soil moisture readings, and Open-Meteo terrain slope data into one clear workspace. For a farmer, this means raw Earth observation data turns into straightforward, on-the-ground help: marking a plot on the map reveals erosion-prone slopes, NDVI layers show where crops are thriving or leaving bare soil, soil moisture and climate readings help time irrigation and save water, and 5-year weather trends highlight upcoming heat, drought, runoff, or frost windows. By pairing those signals with a farmer's current crop practice, irrigation setup, and main goal, FieldShift lays out clear field actions, side-by-side rotation options, and easy answers through Pipori Field Advisor.
